instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Join payments and accounts returning all child rows with parent holder
output: SELECT c.*, p.holder FROM payments c JOIN accounts p ON c.account_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Left join payments to accounts keeping all payments rows
output: SELECT c.*, p.holder FROM payments c LEFT JOIN accounts p ON c.account_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Right join payments to accounts keeping all accounts rows
output: SELECT c.*, p.holder FROM payments c RIGHT JOIN accounts p ON c.account_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Count payments records per holder
output: SELECT p.holder, COUNT(c.id) FROM accounts p LEFT JOIN payments c ON p.id = c.account_id GROUP BY p.holder;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Sum amount per holder
output: SELECT p.holder, SUM(c.amount) FROM accounts p JOIN payments c ON p.id = c.account_id GROUP BY p.holder;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
accounts rows that have no matching payments
output: SELECT p.holder FROM accounts p LEFT JOIN payments c ON p.id = c.account_id WHERE c.id IS NULL;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Full outer join payments and accounts
output: SELECT * FROM payments c FULL OUTER JOIN accounts p ON c.account_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Cross join payments and accounts
output: SELECT * FROM payments CROSS JOIN accounts;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Join and filter payments rows where amount > 100
output: SELECT c.*, p.holder FROM payments c JOIN accounts p ON c.account_id = p.id WHERE c.amount > 100;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Average amount per holder for holder having more than 3 children
output: SELECT p.holder, AVG(c.amount) FROM accounts p JOIN payments c ON p.id = c.account_id GROUP BY p.holder HAVING COUNT(c.id) > 3;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Max amount per holder
output: SELECT p.holder, MAX(c.amount) FROM accounts p JOIN payments c ON p.id = c.account_id GROUP BY p.holder;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Rows joining a city starting with 'N' in holder
output: SELECT c.*, p.holder FROM payments c JOIN accounts p ON c.account_id = p.id WHERE p.holder LIKE 'N%';

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Join with alias and order by amount desc
output: SELECT c.id, p.holder AS detail, c.amount FROM payments c JOIN accounts p ON c.account_id = p.id ORDER BY c.amount DESC;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Left join showing nulls for holder when unmatched
output: SELECT c.*, p.holder FROM payments c LEFT JOIN accounts p ON c.account_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: payments(id, account_id, amount) and accounts(id, holder)
Grouped join returning count and sum together
output: SELECT p.holder, COUNT(c.id) AS cnt, SUM(COALESCE(c.amount,0)) AS tot FROM accounts p LEFT JOIN payments c ON p.id = c.account_id GROUP BY p.holder;
